fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but the Jabbok isn't the river in this passage. The text says they went as far as the Jordan, where they camped before crossing over (Joshua 3:1). Picture a camp this size pulling up to a river, and nobody in line is asking for its name.
Not the Arnon, friend. Joshua 3:1 says they went as far as the Jordan. That's where they camped before crossing over. I mix up my own spice jars all the time, so no shame here.

Yes, Moses. The LORD says He will exalt Joshua so all Israel may know He is with him "…just as I was with Moses." (Joshua 3:7). That's a big thing to hear when you're the one stepping up. I bet Joshua felt every bit of it.

Aaron is a good name to know, but he isn't the one in this line. The LORD says He is with Joshua "…just as I was with Moses." (Joshua 3:7). Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), so I get why he came to mind.

Abraham is a great name, but not the one in this line. The LORD says He will be with Joshua "…just as I was with Moses." (Joshua 3:7). It's Moses the LORD points to here, so that's the name that fits.

Not quite, friend. The LORD says the opposite: "When you reach the edge of the waters, stand in the Jordan." (Joshua 3:8). The priests don't stay on the bank. They go in, and I think that takes a lot of trust.
You've got it, baker. Joshua says to choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, "…one from each tribe." (Joshua 3:12). So it's one man per tribe, not a whole dozen from Levi.

That's the one, baker. Joshua says that when the priests' feet touch down in the Jordan, "…its flowing waters will be cut off and will stand up in a heap." (Joshua 3:13). Water standing up in a heap. If somebody told me that before breakfast, I'd ask them to say it again, slower.
Right, baker. Joshua 3:15 says the Jordan overflows its banks throughout the harvest season. That's high water, not low. I think that makes the walk to the water's edge a serious step.
That's right, friend. Once the water is cut off, "…the people crossed over opposite Jericho." (Joshua 3:16). The river stops and the people cross right across from the city of Jericho.
It's actually true, friend. Joshua 3:16 says the water was cut off, "So the people crossed over opposite Jericho." The crossing happens right across from the city.
Muddy would make for a messy crossing, friend, but the text says the priests stood firm on dry ground (Joshua 3:17). Dry ground, with the whole nation crossing over it. No mud on anybody.
